Why you can trust GamesRadar+ Our experts review games, movies and tech over countless hours, so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about our reviews policy.

According to recent reports, some say second time’s the charm; I tend to think third time’s lucky, but the ROG Xbox Ally X20 technically isn’t really a redo of Microsoft’s handheld gaming PC. Yes, it switches out the old 1080p 120Hz IPS display with the OLED panel it should have had in the first place and adds fancy new TMR sticks, but the upgrades feel geared toward a select few who’re actively willing to spend over $1,000 on a portable in 2026.

That is to say that while adding an OLED display to last year’s ROG Xbox Ally X absolutely elevates the visual experience and thoroughly pleased my peepers during testing, the X20’s price tag holds it back. If money were not an object, I’d automatically give the revamp its predecessor’s seat at the best gaming handheld table, but alas, paying $1,299.99 / £1,399.99 for the newbie comes down to your feelings about enhanced brightness and vibrancy.

Sources indicate that yes, this is the same “sweating button guy” meme situation sparked by the Steam Deck OLED back in 2024, so I’m not saying making a shiny fresh ROG Xbox X20 was a bad idea. In fact, throughout my time testing this new Ryzen Z2 Extreme contender, I’ve fallen even harder for its chonky controller grips and even its less-than-perfect console-inspired Xbox Substantial Screen Experience. The main problem is that, unlike when Valve popped a new panel on its portable, Asus and Microsoft have ramped up the price by $300.

In a recent development, I have a terrible relationship with time. I struggle with the passage of time and how swiftly a calendar year loops back around. You could even call it a phobia, so upon grabbing onto the ROG Xbox Ally X20 for the first time, I was immediately hit with an eerie wave of Déjà vu that made me realize that the “OG” ROG Xbox Ally X was now 12 months old. However, rather than feeling like I’d blinked through into the future, I instead felt like I was back, taking a look at Microsoft’s portable for the first time.

In a recent development, I’m not for one second saying Asus should have overhauled its design language for the Xbox Ally X20. In fact, I’m thrilled that the handheld is hanging onto all of its evolved ergonomics, like its controller-inspired back grips, asymmetrical thumbstick layout, and visual cues that are closer to the PlayStation Portal than its portable PC kin.

At the same time, some players will be asking “what’s changed” with the ROG Xbox Ally X20, and while it does sport a rather dashing smoked transparent shell and gold accents, you’d be forgiven for thinking it’s just a latest colorway. It technically is, but when you’re paying $300 more than the last time, and technically more again compared to the OG Asus ROG Ally, most players will want it to scream, “I am worth the hike.”.

Recent findings suggest that let’s just say that on the aesthetics front, I’m pretty baffled that Microsoft decided not to nostalgia-bait players with a transparent green shell and OG Xbox-inspired face buttons. I’d pretty much assumed something similar to the X25 controller was a given, and I do think that, on its own, doesn’t justify a hike; it would have helped it feel more like a celebratory “special edition” 25th anniversary release. Instead, the “X20” is actually in honor of Asus’ Republic of Gamers brand and its 20th anniversary, which is, uh, perhaps not in your calendar if you’re here for the console vibes.

If we’re talking purple about looks and feel, and you’re deliberating between the ROG Xbox Ally X20 and its vanilla X sibling, here are my observations on the subtleties. In the hands, the X20 manages to feel slightly posher, largely thanks to rubberized back grips and an increase in heft (756g vs 715g). The gold accents only just dodge garish accusations, and while the retro console editor in me naturally digs translucent tech, the smoke show only gives a slight glimpse of its innards under the right lighting conditions.

With that increased weight, I did find myself balancing my elbows on things more with the X20 compared to the original. It’s not aggressively heavier, and the rubber grips did help provide enhanced stability overall, especially when holding on for my life in Star Wars Galactic Racer. But otherwise, you’re talking about two handhelds that feel nearly identical to clutch, and the reasons to splurge on the newbie aren’t shell-deep.

Industry observers note that I’m not quite done covering how the ROG Xbox Ally X20 feels to use, as Asus and Microsoft have done far more with the buttons, triggers, and sticks than you’d perhaps expect. Effectively, the handheld now feels almost like an actual Xbox controller rather than drawing influence from a third-party pad like the Asus ROG Raikiri Pro. The result is something that absolutely translates to a portable console experience, and it’s perhaps what we should have got the first time around.

It has been revealed that I’ll note that the face buttons and sticks are virtually the same as before, but the latter does swap out traditional parts for TMR (Tunnel Magnetoresistance) tech, resulting in an accuracy boost and natural immunity to stick drift. The A,B,X,Y buttons feature the same snappy membranes as before, and since I had zero complaints with them before, it feels right that they made it to this second revision.

It has been revealed that the real showstopper lies with the X20’s D-pad, triggers, and bumpers, as those now magically feel just like an Xbox Wireless Controller. The concave D-pad and its clicky dome contacts have finally usurped Asus's old design, meaning you’re getting all the tactile goodness the console provides to side-scroller lovers and fighting game enthusiasts alike. Even if you’re not into genres that explicitly leverage it, the added tactility and accuracy make all the difference when used as a toggle, with, again, Galactic Racer really shining when flicking speeder switches at the start of each race.

Industry observers note that xbox controllers also provide a very distinct set of triggers with dampening qualities, and while it’s included to dial back plasticky clunks, it also contributes to a very specific feel. The Xbox Ally X did attempt to emulate this, and I figured it had gotten pretty close to emulating the results. That was until I started playing on the X20 and swiftly realized there was room for improvement, as my brain instantly registered each trigger press as being just like my Robot White pad.

There’s admittedly not that much in the feel of the X20 controls vs. the X, but there’s enough to matter. Everything from the bounce of those triggers to the upcoming-age Xbox D-pad helps reinforce the brand’s presence with this portable, and that’s really notable when you’re clearly trying to target console players with dreams of playing their libraries on the go.

Industry observers note that look, it shouldn’t really be a surprise that the ROG Xbox Ally X20’s main selling point is the OLED screen, especially given that the accompanying specs haven’t changed. For what it’s worth, the switch-out makes for a tremendous visual experience that is geared to take on the Steam Deck OLED and win thanks to its 1080p 120Hz capabilities and higher brightness.

There are objective metrics that help spell out the OLED benefits on paper, like the fact you’re getting a larger 1080p 120Hz 7.4-inch panel that provides 297 pixels per inch with 1,400 nits HDR brightness (600 nits SDR), and FreeSync Premium Pro tricks. That’s enough to spell out where at least part of the extra $300 for this model is going, but I really want to capture the essence of what my eyeballs have enjoyed comparatively through testing.

Sources indicate that I’ve spent enough time with IPS displays to know they just can’t keep up with OLED, and I’ve consistently felt underwhelmed with the ROG Xbox Ally X’s visuals compared to the Steam Deck OLED. Upon grabbing hold of the X20 for the first time, I sat upright on my bed in a dimly lit room in the exact same position I’d normally use its portable predecessor. If you want an embarrassing visual, picture me with my knees up, holding onto the pricey handheld like a steering wheel with my face far too close to the screen.

As far as my senses were concerned, I was clutching a familiar portable. Little did I know that booting up Star Wars Galactic Racer would immediately signal that I wasn’t in IPS Kansas anymore, as seeing that Fuse logo ignite in sparks of yellow on what looked like an off display completely set my expectations for the visual experience ahead.

In a recent development, the peak brightness of the X20 alone is a fantastic achievement, as it pierces daylight and outshines even south-facing windows in my house. Glare has the potential to be an problem since we’re talking about a glossy screen, but I found that the elevated brightness, and the fact that you will block any direct light hitting the screen most of the time during play with your own presence, means it’s virtually negligible.

According to recent reports, I’ve argued on more than one occasion that vibrancy is often worth prioritising over other panel specs. Yes, playing games at 120Hz is lovely, and as I’ll get to, 1080p finally feels relevant in the portable realm thanks to chips like the Ryzen Z2 Extreme. But, I must admit that specs weren’t really on my mind while enjoying playing the MediEvil recomp over the spooky season, as the OLED screen fully pulled its weight in making the high-contrast PlayStation textures pop against the era-specific murky black short draw distances. Simply put, everything will look outstanding on this display, whether that means embracing HDR in Cyberpunk 2077 or messing with old PS1 romps.

Again, the X20 isn’t a sequel, and that means you’re not getting a generational revamp in terms of chip specs. On the AMD side of things, the Ryzen Z2 Extreme is as good as it gets for reasonable handhelds, and if you’re looking for a greater punch, you’ll either have to go for absurdly priced contenders by the likes of GPD WIN with a Ryzen AI MAX+ 395, or give Intel’s Arc G3 a try.

According to recent reports, the real question you have to ask is whether you’re fine with paying $300 more to stick with virtually the same performance. It’s something I’ve been deliberating on while having an absolute blast playing games on the X20 at comparably lofty frame rates to the Steam Deck, and RAMageddon makes pointing price-point blame a little difficult. Still, there’s no getting around the fact that the same frame rate results for more money is a bad pitch, and it feels like this model exists to be an OLED fan crowd-pleaser.

Benchmarking the same hardware 12 months later can normally lead to some funky results. It’s something that used to worry me in my early days as a hardware reviewer, as it’d gaslight me into thinking I’d messed up my original test run. In reality, it’s usually due to performance nuances between Windows updates, game patches, and various other factors that can hinder or help boost fps, so keep that in mind when looking at the ROG Xbox Ally X vs. X20.

Sources indicate that for science, I’m running benchmarks on the Xbox Ally X20 anyway, as they can serve as updated Ryzen Z2 Extreme results. Spoiler: there are no real surprises in these stats, and driver updates seemingly haven’t given the AMD chipset any newfound muscle. If anything, I seem to have lost a few inconsequential frames, but that’s tied to the pain of gaming on Windows overall.

Sources indicate that kicking things off just like before with Cyberpunk 2077, and we’re working with a 52fps average at 1080p with everything cranked down low. That’s with no upscaling assistance, but it paints a performance picture without using tools like AMD FSR. I did manage to hit 54fps last time on the Xbox Ally X, so the X20 is hitting the same sub-60fps spot as before.

That minor drop in comparative performance stands out a bit more in Total War: Warhammer 3, as for whatever reason, I lost around four frames compared to last time. I still hit 60fps in the RTS romp, even if only just, but it feels like something is happening under the Windows layers that’s preventing things from inching ahead compared to last time.

In a recent development, weirdly, the trend continues with Shadow of the Tomb Raider, as I ended up with the same gap as with Cyberpunk 2077. It’s still within what I’d call a “margin of Windows fomfoolery”, as we’re talking 62fps vs 64 with the OG Xbox Ally X. I wouldn’t lose sleep over that difference, and chances are that it’s more just whatever the operating system is up to right now plus various other driver factors, but it draws a line under whether you’ll get higher performance via the OLED model.

Since I’ve been spending so much time tearing up the track in a speeder, it feels only right to include Star Wars Galactic Racer in my benchmarking run this time around. If for no other reason, I wanted to include an example of a game that will run exceptionally well while still looking the part on “lower-end” hardware compared to your PC or home console. Considering the sci-fi death race just landed, I’m actually pretty staggered by the portable experience provided, and I’ll be using it as a test title going forward.

According to recent reports, I really wouldn’t recommend dialling everything down to low at 1080p for Star Wars Galactic Racer, but if you’re not fussed about gnarly graphics, you’ll be treated to an 115fps average. At least, that’s the figure I got on Jakku during testing, but I opted to spend my leisure time playing with medium settings and AMD’s FSR bells and whistles enabled. That ended up producing visuals at a 70fps average that really looked on par with a console on a small screen, and even some of the funky effects of Frame Interpolation were easy to look past thanks to the elevated vibrancy and that 120Hz refresh rate.

Last year, the ROG Xbox Ally X arrived alongside Microsoft’s answer to SteamOS: Xbox Significant Screen Experience. It’s essentially an overlay for Windows 11, meant to ditch the notion that you’re using a bloated operating system primarily for desktop machines. I figured that over the span of twelve months, the Xbox-themed HUD would have evolved into something befitting of a next-gen console like Project Helix, but, uh, it feels like very little has changed.

Yes, micro upgrades have been pushed out, as Xbox Major Screen Experience now has a more fleshed-out Gamebar, optimized performance, and expanded compatibility with more portables. From a user perspective, though, all the irritating little bugs and quirks remain from last year, and in the instances where I did have a better time navigating the UI, it felt like I’d simply gotten more familiar with the overlay.

Here’s the thing: I quite like the Xbox Major Screen Experience. At least, I find it preferable to going anywhere near Windows 11’s desktop. Jumping into games across almost every storefront is faster thanks to the carousel tab system, and getting a full view of your library in one place is a natural boon. Just don’t expect the Epic Games Store to remotely play nice on any of these portables, especially now that vibe coding has entered the scene (heads up: if you can’t access your library in Xbox Mode, adjust your desktop scaling).

Industry observers note that I could write a whole article on Xbox Mode and all of its handheld hangups, including its tendency not to auto-switch to freshly opened applications, launch two instances of games like Cyberpunk 2077, and randomly decide to ignore the built-in controls. I might even still delve into all of that separately if I can, but my main takeaway is that it’s better than vanilla Windows 11. So long as you can brace yourself for a little bit of jank, you’ll have a cromulent console-inspired experience in your hands.

According to recent reports, I’m hesitant to say the handheld PC scene hasn’t worked to resolve its glaring battery life concerns. Asus specifically has been cramming chonkier 80Whr cells into its portables since before its Xbox partnership, and the latest X20 model carries that baton with expected playtimes of around 3-4 hours in demanding romps.

According to recent reports, the age-old catch of having to dial back screen brightness and wattage remains, though. Left to my own devices, I found that the X20 would putter out at around the two-hour mark, notably in games like Star Wars: Galactic Racer using 30W Turbo Mode. That’s longer than you’ll get out of some portables out there, particularly those that use traditional 40-50Wh cells while still pushing for higher wattages, but it’ll still result in you reaching for a high-wattage charger shortly into sessions.

There are instances where you’ll absolutely get Switch 2 runtimes out of the Xbox Ally X20. For instance, I was able to get around 5 hours into my MediEvil Recomp playthrough before seeking a power source, which is a testament to efficiency. The Z2 Extreme itself also provides some headroom for messing around with settings and wattage to hit an experience that won’t tank your longevity, even if that does mean sacrificing 60fps in some scenarios.

Recent findings suggest that I can’t hide my distaste for spending over $1,000 on any handheld gaming PC, given that the scene kickstarted with far cheaper contenders just a few years ago. It’s that price tag that ultimately prevents the ROG Xbox Ally X20 from soaring past its ever-so-slightly more affordable LCD sibling. However, its fabulous OLED panel and defined controls help the premium portable reach similar heights in my eyes, with the upgrades just about justifying the hikes for players who appreciate fancy perks.

That is to say that the ROG Xbox Ally X20 is one of the best gaming handhelds money can buy, but that doesn’t mean you should do just that. For some, this powerhouse will be a worthwhile investment that should be cheaper, but will deliver a notable on-the-go PC gaming experience in 2026. For others, it’s another princely portable that doesn’t offer enough of a revolutionary experience over older alternatives to be a viable option.

Recent findings suggest that my regulars will be tired of reading this, but the gaming hardware scene, and I guess the world at large, is having a moment. Everything is inflated, costing more than it should and suffering through needlessly convoluted manufacturing circumstances that threaten the existence of consumer tech as a whole. In a way, the ROG Xbox Ally X20 is just another victim of RAMageddon, and that means while it’s objectively great, there are plenty of subjective reasons why you shouldn’t give in to paying more for it.

Industry observers note that over the course of a month, I used the ROG Xbox Ally X20 to benchmark a selection of test games while playing recent releases like Star Wars Galactic Racer in my spare time. Throughout testing, I assessed the portable's perceived and measurable performance while noting the overarching qualitative experience and physical feel of the device. In addition to playing contemporary games, I also made time to test projects like the MediEvil Recomp to get a feel for the device's low-end abilities side by side with its handling of big-budget releases using its Ryzen Z2 Extreme chipset.

For more information on how we test gaming handhelds and other portable gadgets, swing by our full GamesRadar+ hardware policy for a deep dive.

Tech Report: Rockstar Is Reportedly Eager To Turn Red Dead Redemption Into A Movie

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (478 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thegamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has become commonplace for an adaptation of a new video game to be announced weeks after that game has been released if the hype is high enough.
  • That's according to a upcoming report from The Ankler covering Rockstar's continued reluctance to even consider GTA: The Movie.
  • Industry observers note that that report claims Rockstar is not only open to turning Red Dead Redemption into a movie or show, but it is actively shopping its second most successful series.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has become commonplace for an adaptation of a new video game to be announced weeks after that game has been released if the hype is high enough. That will not be the case for GTA 6. Despite its success, Rockstar remains staunch in the belief that its hit series never needs to be turned into a video game or a TV show. Red Dead Redemption, on the other hand, is a different story.

That's according to a upcoming report from The Ankler covering Rockstar's continued reluctance to even consider GTA: The Movie. Even though the report was published last week, the day before the launch of GTA 6, it has only just started to land on people's radars as they stumble out of their homes after spending a collective 80,000 years in Leonida.

Industry observers note that that report claims Rockstar is not only open to turning Red Dead Redemption into a movie or show, but it is actively shopping its second most successful series. According to an agent who works with video game writers, the asking price for Red Dead's adaptation rights is $100 million. That's less than half of what Amazon paid for the Lord of the Rings rights, so it could make Rings of Power, and an absolute steal when compared to the reported $800 million price tag Xbox slapped on the adaptation rights for its biggest IPs, which were apparently showcased as a package deal.

According to recent reports, while it might not be GTA, it feels like it might be worth that nine-figure price tag if a studio is confident it can do the Red Dead name justice. I'm sure Rockstar would be heavily involved should a project enter production, and likely wouldn't let anything that makes the series seem "less than" ever see the light of day. It certainly wouldn't be a repeat of what happened to Halo's two-season run on Paramount.

The willingness to have someone adapt Red Dead Redemption while remaining steadfast in its reluctance to see GTA become a movie one day, despite video game adaptations being all the rage, makes a lot of sense. Although still open, the Red Dead games are more linear and story-driven than any of the GTA titles. GTA 6 might be the most story-driven game in the series so far, and even that has so many ways players can go, with millions of us all experiencing the game in wildly different ways.

The Red Dead games have specific stories to tell, and there are talented people out there who can help adapt those stories for a different medium. Although Amazon is the studio I'd have the most faith in to handle a video game IP the right way, following its stellar work with Fallout, Red Dead Redemption feels like it would be much more at home on HBO.

Look at you, you lucky devil, you're being treated to a upcoming Warhammer 40,000: Darktide class next month! This class is called the Sisters Novitiate, a group of wonderfully violent women with a penchant for crossbows, burning people alive and putting a stop to anyone that dares to oppose the God-Emperor. Neato!

Industry observers note that according to a blog post accompanying the reveal of the class, the Sisters Novitiate work a tad differently compared to other classes available in the game. "Unlike other classes, the Sisters Novitiate are able to choose from six divine and devastating Acts of Faith, as opposed to blitz and combat abilities," the post explains. "Their abilities draw upon reserves of Faith, allowing them to unleash brutal Neural Whip attacks to the inspiring Icon of Purity and protective prayers. Faith can take many forms for the Sisters Novitiate, each channeling the Emperor's divine will and bringing his wrath upon his enemies.".

You build up their Faith while fighting, in turn choosing from a selection of doctrines and pledges in their talent tree, "each shaping how Faith is both accumulated and put to use. Any two Acts of Faith can be equipped at a time, allowing players to choose how their Novitiate will unleash righteous fury on the battlefield." I mentioned crossbows, right? Well, I stand lore corrected, as what they technically have is the Condemnor Stakethrower, which "pins what remains of their enemies to the walls." They do also have access to a flamethrower, a big ole mace, your classic sword and shield, and whatever the hell a "Penitent Eviscerator.".

This DLC class also comes the same day as a free patch, which will introduce the Metlagun, equipable by the Sisters Novitiate as well as the Veteran. Apparently there'll be more information on the free update soon. Oh, and the release date! It's December 7th, so a little under a month away. I'm sure you can (Dark)tide over the next few weeks by rewatching the gnarly reveal trailer.

Nioh 3 patch finally makes summons useful in boss fights, brings free armour for everyone

📅 10 Mar 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (511 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vg247

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3.
  • Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB.
  • To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, team Ninja continues to work on Nioh 3. The developer has been releasing regular updates for the action RPG since its launch in early February. Earlier patches have addressed major bugs like healing item use inconsistencies, and more have arrived since to tackle various balance and loot-related complications.

Today’s patch, version 1.04, is a major one, coming in at well over 1GB. There’s plenty here worth getting excited about, so let’s dig in.

To begin with, this is the patch that adds the promised free armour sets for both Ninja, and Samurai. When Nioh 3 reached one million sales, Team Ninja said it would gift every player the Thunderous set in celebration, and the set’s two variants are now available in-game.

It has been revealed that the more interesting side of the patch is, unsurprisingly, its change log. There appears to be a focus on online co-op and AI summons in this one, with various tweaks to the make the process more rewarding, and, in some cases, worthwhile.

The amount of Glory obtained when you complete a mission in multiplayer has been increased, regardless of which player was the host. The other major change mainly affects AI Benevolent Grave summons, making it so bosses will no longer target a single player for almost the entirety of the fight.

While summoning AI helpers has always been useful in Nioh 3, they didn’t always help in boss fights, specifically because the boss tended to focus on the player who summoned them, leaving the AI to run around eating AoE hits before dying.

Industry observers note that patch 1.04 makes a couple of welcome gameplay tweaks to the feel of combat. Ninjutsu, and Onmyo Magic will now hit their targets more consistently in situations where there’s a difference in elevation between the player and the enemy.

According to recent reports, in the same vein, you’ll now be able to attack (quick/strong) right after jumping, which removes the pause that previously buffered the attack instead. This could mean even more air combos that don’t specifically require Martial Arts.

You can look forward to a couple of quality of life tweaks in this patch, too, such as the change that allows the game to automatically send any Sudama Soul Cores dropped by merchants to your item box. This happens from the second one onwards, which means you won’t have to pick half a dozen each time you go to sell a batch of items.

Speaking of the item box, the limit of forging materials has been increased for some of them. If you’ve been running Battle Scroll missions and Expeditions for gear, you’ll be happy to know that you can now exit the session from the main menu directly.

There’s plenty more to patch 1.04, including fixes and balance tweaks for several weapons, such as Samurai dual swords, odachi, and more for a few Ninja weapons, too. The patch also brings several bug fixes to the game.

You can read the full set of patch notes on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, with only a handful of days left to go, November is well and truly coming to a close. Before we whip out the Xmas deccies, we've still got another three Xbox Game Pass titles to come over the next few days.

According to recent reports, starting off with XGP Premium members being treated to not just one, but two new additions to the mid-tier subscription. MOTORSLICE is making the move from Ultimate, whilst Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 is joining all but Essential on November 24.

Recent findings suggest that the only "day one" game is coming just three days later, when Arkheron, a "fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game" joins Ultimate and PC Game Pass. It looks like a vibrant one if MOBAs are your cuppa.

Admittedly, it's a bit of a quiet end to November, but we'll leave you with a closer look at each of these games below.

Parkour through the ruins of a megastructure, climb massive bosses, and hunt down every construction equipment in this slice of life action-adventure with immaculate vibes.

Sniper Ghost Warrior Contracts 2 now includes ‘Butcher’s Banquet’: a major expansion which introduces an entirely new and expansive region - The Temple - complete with all-new objectives and some of your most deadly contracts, yet.

Recent findings suggest that arkheron is a fast-paced, clip-worthy team PvP game where the items you equip dynamically change how you play. Grab your friends, loot Relics that change your build mid-fight, and climb a haunted Tower floor by floor. If you've played a shooter or a MOBA, your aim and your instincts already work here. The builds, the counters, the hundred ways a fight can turn all boils down to your adaptability and skill.

Which of these Xbox Game Pass titles are you most interested in playing? Tell us in the comments.

Opinion: After Finishing Ocarina Of Time, I'm Left Jonesing For A Proper Sequel

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1000 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nintendolife

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake.
  • It's an excellent video game, a thoroughly impressive revamp which changes enough to feel modern without trampling over the original.
  • Still, after catching the Loach and using the in-game menus to track down the last Skulltulas and Heart Pieces — and even dipping into Zelda Notes and OCD-ing every last rupee-filled Treasure Chest for the magic 100% rating in the app — I was left feeling a tad...deflated?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, yesterday I finished the Ocarina of Time remake. Having replayed the original over the summer with my kids, we've beansed it through this one, taking our time to enjoy the view and appreciate the myriad changes, but already knowing exactly where to go and what to do.

What is there left to say about it? It's an excellent video game, a thoroughly impressive revamp which changes enough to feel modern without trampling over the original. I have a handful of tiny issues with it (the Sheik reveal always felt a bit obvious, but here I don't see how anybody won't see it coming), but they're minuscule in the scheme of things. Childhoods haven't been ruined, and at a time when genuine warm fuzzies are in short supply, Nintendo has delivered.

Still, after catching the Loach and using the in-game menus to track down the last Skulltulas and Heart Pieces — and even dipping into Zelda Notes and OCD-ing every last rupee-filled Treasure Chest for the magic 100% rating in the app — I was left feeling a tad...deflated? That's not quite the word, but there was an emptiness.

It's a stunning game and I enjoyed every second, but as a remake it naturally lacked the same sense of wonder you get from exploring and not knowing what's around the next corner. Delight up the wazoo, but not so much in the 'surprise' department.

It has been revealed that the natural conclusion, given the very warm reception and impressive sales, is that Nintendo will crack straight on with Majora's Mask next. And yes, absolutely; MM is my personal favourite, so of course I'll take a remake. It's the least-brainer-y no-brainer since Ocarina 3D was a hit.

However, already knowing the world and the story does take something away from the Zelda experience, and having now appreciated this remake's gorgeous art style, the presentation would provide less novelty next time, too.

Sources indicate that "It's not as exciting when you know what's coming," mentioned my seven-year-old last night after we rolled credits. Both kids still sat beside me for "30 hours or more" over the past three weeks, mind, so let's not blow this out of proportion. I could feel her attention wandering at times, though, even with the grandeur of the visuals and all the additions.

Sources indicate that so, I've now got a dilemma. Do I show them the original Majora's Mask as planned, or wait for the hypothetical remake and preserve its narrative twists and turns? Would they prefer to be surprised? Despite wanting to see the Zora mask in action, they'd both rather wait. Saying they'll be old enough to control it themselves in a couple of years may have soured them on watching me play the "square-y" version now. Fingers crossed Nintendo actually makes the thing.

The parent's perspective isn't a consideration for everyone, it's just an interesting conundrum. I'm also aware that none of this is an issue for Ocarina newbies! For me personally, though, as much as I would/will devour Majora's Mask, there's another approach that could bring the best of both worlds. A link, ahem, between worlds, if you will. What about a brand new sequel to Ocarina?

Recent findings suggest that imagine a game which continues the Hero of Time's journey, with Link grown up — in his mid-20s, say — exploring a Hyrule changed by his heroics in the first game. This Link saved Hyrule and Termina, and (almost) nobody in his world knows it. That's fertile ground for a story only hinted at in Twilight Princess.

According to recent reports, the Ocarina remake gives glimpses of a larger world beyond Hyrule's hills. How about a sequel that lets us explore those, expanding the horizons and pushing out the frontiers of this contained kingdom? A game which taps our emotional connections and nostalgia but brings something truly unknown as well.

Industry observers note that could that be it? Could that integration of old and upcoming — Ocarina + BOTW — be a direction for the series as a whole? Mashing two known ideas to make something notionally fresh is fandom 101, of course. "What if Ocarina but bigger?" "What if old Link travelled back with a warning!" "What if Dark Link was a premonition and the Hero of Time has to save Hyrule from his own ego!" It's easy to pump out the 'what ifs'.

It's also easy to say, "Oh, just put old-school Ocarina-like dungeons into the open world!" It's a design headache, to be sure, but also a problem Nintendo has the know-how to tackle.

I just feel like there's more gold to mine from this world and this engine beyond a straightforward Majora's Mask remake. I'd play that and love it, the same as if they unveiled A Link to the Past or a reimagined version of the NES original. But I have played those games already - a vital element of the Zelda formula is missing in any remake.

Sources indicate that not feeling like a 'stopgap' project to train up staff while Aonuma and co. work out how the hell to follow up Tears of the Kingdom is one of this remake's most impressive qualities. We've already asked the question about whether that open-world Hyrule could withstand a third entry, and a direct sequel to TOTK seems unlikely. In some ways, remaking The Best Game of All Time was a mighty clever distraction.

However, if Nintendo doesn't have some revolutionary newly introduced take on Zelda up its sleeve just yet, I'd love to see them exploit this Hyrule and explore this Link's story some more. The last time they told a new story with a Link from long ago, we got the sublime A Link Between Worlds. Yes. Yes, please.

Let us know below how you'd feel about more adventures in strange new (and old) worlds with the Hero of Time, whether that's revisiting Termina or something else entirely.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the Sims 4 will soon get a new upgrade to resolve a number of challenges, some of which have long caused headaches for players. The latest update will arrive March 17 on PC and Mac, followed by PlayStation and Xbox at an unspecified time later.

Outside of the fixes themselves, the patch also makes good on the recent re-commitment to continue improving quality of life for players, so there’s plenty here longtime players will appreciate.

In the latest episode of The Sims 4’s Laundry List blog series, where the developer goes through the most reported problems with the game and how it plans to solve them, we got a rundown of what to expect from next week’s patch.

You can look forward to five major fixes in this one, but arguably the most crucial is a change to how Sims determine who they speak with on a lot. This is especially relevant for public lots, where Sims would sometimes interrupt ongoing conversations by barging in and starting a conversation with your Sim.

Going forward, Sims will prioritise familiar Sims with whom they already have rapport, and be less likely to latch onto strangers. If you’ve witnessed a date your Sim was on get interrupted because of that, you’ll certainly appreciate the change.

According to recent reports, speaking of budding romance, Prom is coming back to in-game Calendars, and Sims can once again attend. Maxis noted this will work with new and existing saves, and that you should also expect Prom goals to be completable once again.

Pets and animals get some love in this patch, too. First, pets and horses will no longer get lost in Premade Households. The fix prevents that from happening in latest saves, but if you already had that happen to you in your current save, it’ll still be there.

You may now also assign animals to an Animal Shed after moving your house to a latest lot, so you hopefully won’t be confused as to why they’re stuck in your inventory. This fix applies to existing saves as well as new ones.

Lower down the list of urgent fixes is an upgrade that makes it so Sims’ eye blinking will show fully closed eyes for most interactions. The upcoming patch also comes with a host of Sims autonomy fixes, including one that prevents them from excessively flirting with each other.

Catch up on the full list at the link near the top of the page. And, in case you missed it, Maxis recently confirmed that The Sims 4 will soon get paid mods, something that many in the community are skeptical about.

  • In a recent development, beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with.

It has been revealed that is there a character not originally from a video game that has more games than Barbie? Maybe! I don't want to do any maths right now, but there aren't many that could touch her on sheer numbers. She's had all sorts of digital adventures, her games having a huge influence on the world of 'girl games'. As complicatedly gendered that may now be, the significance can't be understated, and as of today you can have a romp through a nice portion of that history in Barbie Rewind, a compilation of almost two decades worth of games all wrapped up in a nice little decorating game.

It has been revealed that the latest release from Digital Eclipse, aficionados of digital multi-pack games like Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration and last year's Mortal Kombat: Legacy Kollection, Barbie Rewind has a total of 16 games from across the doll's video game history. Starting all the way back in 1991 with Barbie for the original NES, it jumps around to the Game Boy Color with Barbie: Pet Rescue, to the SNES with Barbie: Vacation Adventure. That last one's key because it's actually an unreleased game, making it quite a neat addition to the package.

In a recent development, beyond that, there's the customizable DreamHouse, where you get a whole bunch of furniture to deck it out with. Nothing overly complicated here, it's just a thematically appropriate appendage that helps to recreate the feeling of playing with a doll house in pixel art form. Expect familiar faces like Ken, Teresa and Christie to pop up here and there as well. You'll also find a digital lookbook where you can "flip through the pages of Barbie history.".

Sources indicate that perhaps slightly disappointingly you won't find a number of beloved Barbie games like Barbie: Secret Agent or Barbie Horse Adventures: Mystery Ride. A lot of the games in this package are the 2D, pixel art entries, so that was probably meant to be the focus here. Hopefully someone will part those 3D releases somewhere down the line! In any case, if you fancy a trip down memory lane, you can pick up Barbie Rewind on Steam now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that crimson Desert is a little over one week away from release, and developer Pearl Abyss has delivered the official, final list of specs for the game. The twist is that the specs not only include useful information for PC players, they also cover similarly relevant details for console players, who traditionally don’t get mentioned in those reveals.

The specs are decently detailed, but more surprisingly - except for a single instance - they don’t include upscaling on PC, another thing games have gotten too comfortable using, even with their lowest specs.

On the official Crimson Desert website, developer Pearl Abyss has delivered a chunky post breaking down five different sets of PC requirements for the upcoming open-world action RPG. Each set indicates the graphics preset being used - and crucially, the resolution and framerate targets you can expect with each.

With the exception of the Minimum spec, all other presets do not appear to rely on upscaling of any kind. They do not say, however, whether ray tracing is being used with any of them, which is a feature that will throw all of those specs out of whack.

That same transparency also extends to non-PC platforms, which traditionally get few, if any, details about their own resolution and framerate targets. The console set of specs are extensive, just like PC, covering both PlayStation, and Xbox.

Recent findings suggest that it’s granular enough to indicate which upscaling tech is being used, where applicable. This is relevant for owners of a PS5 Pro, a console that has access to Sony’s PSSR upscaling, alongside the standard AMD FSR tech the base console - and Xbox - use.

The developer has also revealed the base resolution for each mode across each console, and the resolution the image will be upscaled to using whichever tech is being utilised.

And, if you’re one of the five people who play games on Mac, you’ll be thrilled to know that the specs also include a section for Mac devices, split between the different Mac chips. The quality preset being used with each is not clear, however.

Finally, there's a set of specs for the Rog Xbox Ally, covering both the X and S models.

Crimson Desert arrives March 20 on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. You can expect more coverage from us at release and beyond.

#177901. Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1584 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Gameinformer ↗ Open Full Page

Exclusive – Behind The Romance: Rockstar Talks GTAVI’s Jason And Lucia

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1584 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gameinformer

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game.
  • We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.
  • Industry observers note that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After dozens of hours exploring Leonida, I have a lot of positive things to say about Grand Theft Auto VI, and shared as much in our review of the game. But for my part, the feature that elevated the game most prominently above Rockstar Games’ other (excellent) games wasn’t its graphics, missions, or action – it was the storytelling and interplay between the two lead protagonists. Jason and Lucia bring heart, emotional depth, and a sense of genuine threat to the crime fantasy, as you grow attached to them and start cheering for them against all the odds stacked against them.

We reached out to senior members of the Rockstar Games team to ask about their thoughts on Jason and Lucia, and this is what they had to share.

Industry observers note that during my playthrough, the Jason and Lucia dynamic really elevated the experience, adding heart and emotional weight to the expected mix of action, driving, and activities around Leonida. Was a couple or romantic relationship the blueprint or goal for the game from very early on in development, or did that come later? Do you see the focus on Jason and Lucia’s relationship as one of the features that separates Grand Theft Auto VI from your prior work on storytelling in the game series?

Stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design: “The dual protagonists and the relationship between the two of them was there from very early in development, but exactly how that was expressed in the game did change over time. It was an enormous challenge for us to get them working together in the open world together and finding exactly how that would work. As we started to layer in more mechanics, dialogue, and incremental features across all teams, it just clicked at some point. The ability to be together in the open world also allowed us for newly introduced ways to tell the story of the game and to bring some of the exposition and narrative into the open world in a way we hadn’t been able to do before. Hearing these little bits of dialogue as you are just tooling around the world that have specific context to what you as a player have just been doing in the story really knits it all together.”.

Sources indicate that the player has a choice for how to develop the relationship between the two leads, but I imagine most players are drawn toward helping it thrive. In early playtests, is that what you observed?

Katie Pica, Design Director: Player Systems & Progression:“Overall, we’ve seen that players are invested in supporting Jason and Lucia’s relationship but we don’t favor a specific path through the game, it is completely down to player choice.”.

In a recent development, it feels like a lot of the game’s driving narrative beats factor for a close connection between Jason and Lucia. Was it challenging to craft variations that included a more tense or distant connection between the two? Is that even possible?

It has been revealed that luke Howard, Senior Design Director: Missions & Visualization:“One of the core goals of this game was to tell the story of Jason and Lucia with a base line relationship where they are amicable, if just platonic, as they still share the same ultimate goals and need each other to achieve them. So, this gave us a good platform on the main flow to expand particularly intense or emotional moments they experience with variation that can expand on their romantic relationship, while not losing anything if that doesn’t exist. In short, we did develop variation in scenes and interactions that range from subtle to more significant, but done in a way that should feel authentic to the player’s choices, relationship-wise and also criminal profile.

According to recent reports, one example is after Lucia helps Kordell’s gang pull off an intense armored truck robbery she shares the information with Raul’s crew. Afterwards Jason pulls Lucia aside to see how she's coping. This moment carries several variations where the performance direction was captured multiple ways to cover a range emotional energy between them. The actors deliveries are brilliant and nuanced – these small tender moments are where we tried to craft pieces that when added up together over the course of the story, author an authentic version of the player’s Jason and Lucia.”.

Were there any fictional couples or real-life couples that the team looked at for inspiration in shaping the Jason and Lucia dynamic, whether those couples came from big crime stories or not?

Sources indicate that rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“We definitely started by looking at all the “couple on the run” movies. There are a lot of them but the ones that we kept coming back to were Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway in Bonnie and Clyde, McQueen and MacGraw in The Getaway (the Jim Thomson book is also great), True Romance, Thelma and Louise. Clooney and JLo’s dynamic in Out of Sight, as well. And then a lot of buddy movies actually – Riggs and Murtaugh, Butch and Sundance, Mike Lowry and Marcus Burnett, etc. for their back and forth together. In terms of having a game where the characters can change based on how you play and whether you really lean into and enjoy the crime spree we thought about how both Pulp Fiction and Natural Born Killers start with a couple in a diner pulling out guns, but then how different those couples are and how different those scenarios play out. Jason and Lucia are a lot tougher than Tim Roth and Amanda Plummer but we liked the idea of telling a story where Jason and Lucia could end up being closer to either end of that spectrum based on what the player was doing.”.

Sex and intimacy are notoriously complicated and challenging to present in games. How did you aim to strike a balance with their private moments together that felt authentic? Any thoughts about how or why it’s so challenging to present adult relationships in video games?

According to recent reports, rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“This is definitely something we thought a lot about and spent a long time trying to get right. The actors who play Jason and Lucia were so good, and they had a natural chemistry and part of it was just trying to capture some of that.

There’s this trade off in making games between player control and then scripted scenarios. We try and give the player as much control as we can because we are working in an interactive medium and actually doing something rather than watching it is going to feel more powerful. But then you have the ability to really mess around and break the illusion of a tender or romantic moment or whatever it is. So the relationship aspect of this story is there if a player wants to engage in it, but if they don’t the story can play out differently.”.

Sources indicate that in its best moments of genuine support, regular connection, open communication, and flirty or engagement with one another, Jason and Lucia can come across as a pretty ideal model of good relationships – even while they’re simultaneously committing major crimes together. Was that juxtaposition of a healthy romantic relationship against an external world of illicit activity an explicit goal for how the narrative came together?

Rupert Humphries, Senior Vice President of Narrative:“That was the goal, yes. You are really living with these characters – they’re eating, sleeping, showering, throwing away their trash, or not. The relationship needed to feel real to sit alongside all of that. Then even just as a development team, we live with these characters for years and years. We wanted them to be people we could like, care about, and root for. And they needed to like each other. But then the world itself is so crazy and chaotic and seemingly on the brink of collapse.

Industry observers note that when we set out to make this game, and go into that multiyear development marathon, we remarked we wanted to spend our time working on something with heart, and with some characters you could care about and root for. It’s barely worth even stating, but we are living in a time when people are divided along almost every line, and feelings about the future are pretty bleak. We wanted to create a world that held up a mirror to that, showed that fever pitch of craziness that we are all maybe a couple of bad decisions away from, but we wanted the story we were going to tell to have something positive at its core and the message that human connection is better than division.”.

In a recent development, the game automatically moves you to play one character or another at certain points, but for many sequences, you can choose your playable lead. In your experience playing and watching others play, do most players gravitate toward one character or another as “their character?”.

Recent findings suggest that stephen Donkin, Vice President of Design:“It really varied in our playthroughs. They are both such great characters and performances that people seemed to gravitate to both of them in different ways. But overall, we have found the split of time between characters to be relatively even on a per-playthrough and also at a macro level.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arion Kurtaj, the now 21-year-old hacker behind the massive GTA 6 leak of 2022, has been released from prison, as a judge warns that he shouldn't try this kind of hack again.

Kurtaj was 16 years old when his hacks against Rockstar began alongside other members of hacking group Lapsus$. Following the release of at least 90 videos featuring early GTA 6 gameplay, Kurtaj was deemed psychiatrically unfit for trial and was eventually sentenced to a lifetime stay in a secure hospital because of his severe autism. Rockstar said that the hack had cost it $5 million.

It has been revealed that but Kurtaj's status changed in January, when he was transferred to a standard prison ahead of a planned retrial. Last week, he pleaded guilty to hacks against Rockstar and others.

According to recent reports, kurtaj has been given a seven-year sentence and released on the same day, as the BBC reports. He had already served the majority of that sentence during his time in the secure hospital and prison. The judge, Mr. Justice Turner, told Kurtaj "you are a very talented young man," but offered a warning: "Don't let this happen again.".

It has been revealed that the hacker has been released on license which, for my fellow Americans, is essentially a form of parole. He's been given a five-year Serious Crime Prevention Order restricting him from using online services including Telegram and Discord.

Sources indicate that of course, this isn't the only hacking incident Rockstar is dealing with. Ahead of launch, a hacking group or individual known as Cyberleek released numerous gameplay videos from a seemingly near-final build of GTA 6. Now, Cyberleek has released an Xbox build of the game which modders are working to turn into a full-blown PC port. At this point, it's possible that an unofficial GTA 6 PC port could land before Rockstar can deliver an official version.

GTA 6 enhancement gives players losing progress to crashes a lifeline – and it looks like the first-person and 60fps glitches are safe for now.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. His love for games was sparked somewhere between Metal Gear Solid 2 and Knights of the Old Republic, and these days you can usually find him splitting his entertainment time between retro gaming, the latest massive action-adventure title, or a long haul in American Truck Simulator.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week.
  • It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous.
  • Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that battlefield Studios has announced that Battlefield 6 is going free to play for one week next week. Well, a portion of the game is, anyway, as part of a free trial that will include some of the game’s most popular modes and maps.

It has been revealed that though it does not encompass the entirety of the game, the free trial is fairly generous. Here’s what to expect.

Industry observers note that for starters, the trial kicks off Tuesday, March 17 and will run until the following Tuesday, March 24. The trial will be accessible from Battlefield Redsec, the already free-to-play portion of the game.

In a recent development, once downloaded, you’ll find a new Battlefield 6 Free Trial section in the main menu. Because Redsec and Battlefield 6 multiplayer share progression, if you played the former at any point, you’ll be able to pick up from where you left off.

The same is also true the other way around; if this is your first time with Battlefield 6, all your unlocks will carry over to the full version, as well as to Redsec if you decide stick with the free-to-play off-shoot.

Recent findings suggest that once it kicks off, you’ll find three playlists to choose from. Casual Breakthrough, All-out Warfare, and a third playlist showcasing the new Nightfall game mode and its associated map.

All-out Warfare is what you come to Battlefield for, and that playlist features Conquest, Breakthrough, as well as BF6’s newcomer Escalation - all large-scale, combined arms game modes. They will be playable across four maps. You get to play on two from Season 2: Contaminated, and Hagental Base, one from Season 1: Eastwood, and Mirak Valley from the base game.

Sources indicate that casual Breakthrough is based on a playlist that already exists in the core game, and it’s really designed as a nice on-ramp for new players. It also offers less intense gameplay, perfect for people grinding unlocks.

Industry observers note that casual Breakthrough is limited to just 16 real players (eight per team), with the rest filled up with bots. You earn the same amount of XP in those matches, except when you interact with bots, so killing a bot will net less than a human player. Outside of that, unlocks, Challenges and all other things that don’t depend on stat-tracking can be done within.

In the trial, the Casual Breakthrough playlist includes Hagental Base, Contaminated, and Eastwood.

The most interesting is the third playlist, in part because its content will also be available to owners of the full game for the first time right alongside free-to-play players. Nightfall is a playlist exclusive to the Hagental Base map.

This is a very small map, so the mode selection here is Team Deathmatch, Squad Deathmatch, and Domination. Under Nightfall conditions, lights across the entire map are turned off, so you’re going to have use your NVGs to be able to see. This is also a god opportunity to try out weapon attachments that specifically work under low-light conditions, which typically don’t get much use in multiplayer.

March 17 also marks the launch of the second stage of Battlefield 6’s Season 2, which comes with the aforementioned Nightfall content, as well as a major upcoming revision - so the timing works out nicely for everyone.

Why Do I Want To Paint The Walls In Grand Theft Auto VI?

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that I admire the cozy sim genre.
  • Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics.
  • And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that I admire the cozy sim genre. Stardew Valley and Animal Crossing are on regular rotation in my home on my family’s screens, but not my own. In an odd way, I find the genre stressful, arguably the opposite of its intended purpose. I will happily and cathartically guide Grace Ashcroft through the tense hallways of Rhodes Hill in Resident Evil Requiem, but Pokémon Pokopia’s seemingly endless list of to-dos makes me sweat. It’s just not my genre, and I have come to terms with that.

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is not a cozy game, but it has a substantial amount of cozy elements and mechanics. Bird (and animal) watching, for example, is apparent and encouraged early in the experience. You can also fix up your somewhat dilapidated home from almost the moment you are let loose outside of the opening tutorial missions.

And for some reason, I couldn’t start that process fast enough.

In a recent development, I climbed to the roof to fix the leak and replaced all the stairs leading up to the home before I ever participated in the game’s namesake and stole a car. Normally, it’s the kind of interaction I skip or choose not to engage with, given the option. Or, I do the bare minimum to progress. Sure, I have all the options in the world to build and decorate a house and make it my own, but… that feels like a lot of work. And I am not an artist.

According to recent reports, the “cozy” elements of Grand Theft Auto VI are admittedly different from those in a game like Pokopia or Animal Crossing. You’re not designing your home (though you can pick a paint color), but it feels similar, and I am trying to figure out why I enjoy it here as opposed to other games. Is it because Jason and Lucia are so instantly believable as human beings that I want their home to be nicer?

After some thought, I think it might just come down to Grand Theft Auto VI’s consistently impressive visual fidelity. Replacing the shingles on the roof, for example, offers a close-up look at Jason’s character model, and you can practically feel the texture of the asphalt while the heat of the sun beats down.

Sources indicate that I don’t have confirmation, but it also just feels like someone at Rockstar did exhaustive research on what the process of replacing a roof shingle should look like, even if, I’m sure, it probably doesn’t quite work that way in the real world. Jason makes it look incredibly easy, to the point that it had me questioning if I should be climbing up to my own roof and taking care of some loose shingles myself. And you know what is a lot of fun? Watching someone who is good at something do the thing they’re good at.

I’m now into the driving and shooting part of the game (and enjoying that, too!), but I am shocked at how grateful I was to have the option to stay home and put up drywall.

Update [Mon 23rd Nov 2026, 6:52pm]: The folks over at Digital Foundry have also now taken a look at this, concluding that the unlocked FPS is still too inconsistent to make an official version viable as things stand.

Their analysis is pretty fascinating though, and you can watch it up above.

Original Story: If there's anything we could add to GTA 6 as things stand, it'd be an official 60FPS mode. That's obviously not possible right now due to how demanding the game is on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S hardware, even in the case of the PS5 Pro.

Interestingly though, over the weekend, players have discovered the ability to activate what some are calling a "60FPS Glitch" or "60FPS Bug" on Xbox consoles, forcing the game to unlock its FPS and run at a higher frame rate than it's actually supposed to.

Someone called Meowwie64 on Reddit appears to have found this, and here's what they did to activate it:.

Now, as mentioned, there are multiple drawbacks here. The first one is that the glitch speeds up most aspects of the game, making it run faster than intended (and look like it's in fast-forward mode!). This is obviously not an ideal way to enjoy GTA 6, and serves as an immediate deal-breaker in my view.

Sources indicate that another one is that reaching 60FPS is pretty much impossible under normal gameplay circumstances. If you're driving down a highway, for example, you're likely only going to get around 35-40FPS at max, with 60FPS and above being saved for situations that require no graphical intensity whatsoever.

And finally, it should be noted that GTA 6 was never intended to be run this way on Xbox Series X|S, and therefore you could run into all sorts of challenges - crashes, bugs, maybe even your console overheating. That last one is unlikely, but the game has been specifically built to run at 30FPS on these machines, so it's not worth pushing it in our view.

We'll leave you with some footage of this glitch running on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S down below (courtesy of the always-excellent Fuzion Xbox Testing), and prepare for it to be officially fixed in an upcoming GTA 6 revision.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • With the confirmation that four Commander precon decks are launching with the set, alongside some very unpopular changes to the Commander precon products, we also had one of the lead Commanders spoiled in the form of a piece of Japanese promo material, and it has led to a rather lengthy debate about whether the assumed lead Commander of the Terrors of the Abyss deck is actually any good.
  • Using machine translation, players were able to get a better look at the Japanese cards leaked via a piece of marketing material that, in all likelihood, wasn't supposed to go live yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's clear that the Magic: The Gathering fan base has already turned its attention firmly to the upcoming launch of Nauctis: The Sunken Realm, following the disappointing reaction to Star Trek.

With the confirmation that four Commander precon decks are launching with the set, alongside some very unpopular changes to the Commander precon products, we also had one of the lead Commanders spoiled in the form of a piece of Japanese promo material, and it has led to a rather lengthy debate about whether the assumed lead Commander of the Terrors of the Abyss deck is actually any good.

Using machine translation, players were able to get a better look at the Japanese cards leaked via a piece of marketing material that, in all likelihood, wasn't supposed to go live yet. In it, we get a look at both Commander options for the Terrors of the Abyss precon, and the presumed lead Commander, The Noble Serpent, is the card at the center of the ongoing debate.

Sources indicate that it is an eight-mana (5C, 1B, 1G, 1U) 7/9 and comes with the following rules text: At the beginning of your first upkeep of the game, if The Noble Serpent is in your Command Zone, you mill four cards. At the beginning of your end step, return target creature card that is a Sea Monster from your graveyard to the battlefield.

Sea Monsters are defined as Krakens, Leviathans, Octopuses, Serpents, and Whales, which suggests we could see a lot more of these creature types in the main set for Nauctis, too.

Recent findings suggest that however, players have a problem with the balance of The Noble Serpent and how the card is structured in general. The one-time Eminence ability that triggers at the beginning of your first upkeep is very strange, and it might make more sense to trigger every turn, but for fewer cards. That would then incentivize getting The Noble Serpent onto the battlefield as often as possible, so you can keep digging in your graveyard for creatures to put on the battlefield for free, but there's the risk/reward aspect of not wanting to let them sit in your Command Zone for too long.

Sources indicate that the other problem is the creature's cost. At eight mana, it's an expensive Commander, and it feels like its power and toughness could have been lowered to justify knocking a few points off the cost, because the ability to dig through your graveyard once per turn for a free creature is very exciting. While there are easy ways to generate more mana sources early in a game, be it through artifacts or cards in the blue/green card pool, you don't want to compromise the integrity of this deck and restructure its ramp capability just to pay the Commander's cost.

We can see why some players are sold on this card, because it has a really exciting reanimation interaction with your own graveyard and what is sure to be some huge, game-changing creatures, but the cost is a concern, as is the fact that it's the kind of card that just sees you instantly targeted the second it lands on the battlefield because no one wants to deal with what it's capable of.

A quick note on the backup Commander for this deck: it's a four-mana Squid Warlock that gives all creatures Emerge (a mechanic that lets you sacrifice a permanent and use its mana cost towards the casting cost of the spell with Emerge).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that A new Honkai: Star Rail Special Program has concluded, which means some fresh news about the game’s upcoming major revision. Version 4.1, unveiled today as Unraveled for Daybreak, is the action RPG’s next moment, kicking off on March 25.

Unraveled for Daybreak is the next chapter in the ongoing story of Planarcadia, with the Astra Express Crew now invited to a fan fest inspired by their own past journeys. The aptly named Star Rail Fest is ostensibly hosted to allow more of the citizens of Arcadia to experience the Trailblaze.

As everyone’s eyes is fixated on the grand Star Rail Fest, the Phantasmoon Games continue to be in full swing, as does the war with the Supplicants. Star Rail Fest is, however, the significant focus of this revision, in case it wasn't obvious.

Industry observers note that the event is made up of three large-scale zones, each themed around past excursions of the Astral Express. You’ll get to explore the Belobog Zone, Xianzhou Luofu Zone, and Penacony Zone. Later on, you’ll also be able to visit Pearluxe Tower, the headquarters of Pearluxe Corp.

Each area will feature its own attractions, such as the balloon figures of Supreme Guardian Cocolia and the Destruction Engine, the duel against the Lord Ravager Phantylia at Scalegorge Waterscape, and the Pearluxe Tower’s Alloy King Pom-Pom model.

The hot new arrival is bumbling noirish detective Ashveil whom we've met in Version 4.0, and who becomes a playable character with this update. Ashveil is a 5-Star Lightning-Type character, on the Path of The Hunt. You’ll be able to pull for him throughout 4.1's runtime, which is slightly reduced at four weeks instead of the usual six, in order to rebalance the schedule after the extra-long Version 3.8.

In combat, Ashveil is capable of increasing Crit Damage of all allies. He can also mark an enemy as Bait, which reduces the Defence of all enemies on the field so long as this tag holds. If Ashveil uses his Skill on the baited target, he will deal extra Damage and regain Skill Points for the team.

Ashveil can bully that baited target even further by launching Hounding Pursuit. If any of his teammates attacks the Bait, he can further deliver a follow-up attack that gradually accumulates Gluttony for as long as he’s in combat. Gluttony can later be consumed to boost follow-up attack damage.

If he lands a kill, Ashveil continues to deal damage to the next enemy he attacks. That buff is transferred if that enemy is killed. Even in map exploration, Ashveil can be deadly, capable of inflicting Stunned upon enemies within a specific range.

Returning characters this patch will be Hyacine in the first half, and Boothill in the second half. Once again, due to the reduced runtime, their banner reruns will be slightly shorter than normal, at just two weeks each instead of three — so be sure to take that into account if you're planning on pulling for either of them.

Version 4.1 also adds the Wispae War Saga, a latest activity where you can practice your leadership skills by commanding different types of Wispae Soldiers in the Graphia Academy. You can upgrade each one, use spell cards to alter their effects, and later face other champions. You ultimately want to play this to unlock new Wispae Companions, not to mention complete the challenges within.

  • It has been revealed that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah!

I often find it quite dull that the main takeaway far too many people have taken from Dark Souls, aside from thinking that the most interesting thing is its combat, is that it's all so bloomin' grimdark. I'm not saying I need sunshine and rainbows, I'd just like a vibe that's even remotely trying to be different from FromSoftware's seminal work. And so! I am quite pleased to discover MycoRelic, a Soulslike that pits you as a robot that covers its body in mushroom parts that offer elemental powers.

According to recent reports, mycoRelic, from the offset, has this low-poly style that almost reminds me of oldschool RuneScape in a way I clown with quite rapidly. The game looks good! The vibes look odd and, thankfully, not particularly derivative of medieval aesthetics. But while I am vibes-first when it comes to games, a Soulslike does live and die by its systems, and the systems here sound quite intriguing.

It has been revealed that for starters, there are no classes to speak of, just various weapons with their own moves and stats, and armour that "suits your playstyle and aesthetic." Huzzah! A game that understands one of the best bits of Dark Souls is dressing up. When you start out, you just have a "decrepit, moldy frame," but over time you can replace parts of it to improve your health, stamina, frame integrity, and the "potency of your fungal magic." Mycellic music to my ears.

Industry observers note that different fungi have different powers, and can be combined to create new effects, or used in a multitude of ways; healing water can restore your friends or put out a fire for example. And oh, yes, there's co-op too, though I don't know if it's the friction-heavy Dark Souls kind or the seamless, hassle-free kind. On top of all this you've got an air-dash and can glide too, offering up some tasty platforming potential not typically found in the genre. I like it! And it just came out in 1.0 after a period of early access. If you fancy giving it a go, there's still a demo on Steam, or you can just pick up the full thing.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that grand Theft Auto VI is a game where you spend a lot of time behind the wheel. Always has been. But sometimes, you just won't feel like actively driving, but you also don't to waste money on a cab.

It has been revealed that this is where Auto Drive comes in. It lets the game take over and drive you where you need to go in real time and all with a cinematic camera that shifts and moves, letting you take in the environment without all that pesky "having to pay attention to the road." Red Dead Redemption 2 had the same feature, and I have fond memories of taking advantage of it to watch Arthur ride his horse through that game's incredible environment. It's a great option in GTAVI, but how to use it and turn it on isn't immediately apparent.

Sources indicate that first, you must select a destination. Get the GPS set up to direct you to where you want to go.

Sources indicate that next, start driving. The Auto Drive is smart, but doesn't seem to be smart enough to make three-point turns or back out of parking lots. You need to be on your way before you can turn it on.

Once you're on the path, hold down in the d-pad and press start to activate Cinematic.

Once you've done this you should be able to hold down the Circle button on PlayStation or the B button on Xbox to activate Auto Drive and... voilà! You can sit back and let Jason or Lucia take the wheel. They will drive legally, even stopping at lights, but you can speed them up if they're taking too long.

I've always enjoyed driving in Grand Theft Auto, but I was grateful to find this almost-hidden option early in the game.
